data.what: P1-a (hosted-UI OAuth scope) is REFUTED for the mobile app and needs no fix. The review claimed getUser 401s for Google/Apple customers because hosted-UI tokens cannot carry aws.cognito.signin.user.admin. Verified against source: both apple-oauth.ts and google-oauth.ts mint the tokens they hand the client via ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH (apple-oauth.ts:490,575,769,845; google-oauth.ts:716,811), not the hosted-UI /oauth2/token exchange. Cognito API auth flows issue the admin scope, so getUser works.
data.why: A release blocker that is not real would have stalled 2.1.0 for nothing; the claim was checkable in one grep and the source contradicts it.
data.costIfWrong: If some untraced path DOES return a hosted-UI token to the mobile client, those users 401 on the route and the customer-app client silently refresh-retries the deletion body until it force-logs-out.

data.what: P1-b (isOAuthUser is dead) is CONFIRMED and is the real Apple 2.1.0 release blocker, and I am NOT fixing it in this phase. Native Apple/Google accounts are created by adminCreateUser with username=email, custom:role set, and a RANDOM permanent password via adminSetUserPassword (apple-oauth.ts:443-468) - they carry no 'identities' attribute, so isOAuthUser is false and the route demands a password the user was never told. They cannot delete their account.
data.why: A correct fix needs a trustworthy signal for 'this account has no user-known password', and the backend has none: user_mgmt.identities has no provider column (cognito_sub, primary_email, timestamps only), commerce.customers has none, and adding a Cognito custom: attribute is forbidden by aws-change-control. The one attribute that correlates - custom:role, set by the OAuth paths and deliberately unset by password signups - attests WHICH ROLE the account is, not whether it has a known password. Inferring the latter from it is the exact error class that produced both P0s in this phase (the URL path, then cognito:groups): using an attribute as evidence for something it does not attest. I will not make it a third time unattended.
data.costIfWrong: 2.1.0 ships without a working deletion path for Sign in with Apple users, which is precisely the population guideline 5.1.1(v) is about, and App Review rejects it.

data.what: P1-c (the erasure leaves identities.primary_email, device_tokens, web_push_subscriptions and crm.contacts behind while the response says 'Your account has been deleted') is confirmed and deferred. Not fixed here.
data.why: Completing it is a DB-content change across four schemas plus a decision about what 'deleted' promises, and the safe form is constrained: identities.primary_email must be scrubbed IN PLACE because hetzner/shim/jit/index.ts gates JIT on identities.cognito_sub - deleting the row re-opens JIT and cognito-post-confirmation's upsert writes the PII back. That is a designed change with its own migration rail, not a tail fix on a deploy.
data.costIfWrong: A customer who deletes their account remains re-identifiable by a one-join lookup on an indexed real email, and keeps a live push channel to their handset.

data.what: STOPPING code changes to delete-account.ts. The independent review of my own #174 fix found FOUR regressions I introduced in that single unattended pass: (1) the INCORRECT_PASSWORD 400 at :199 is thrown inside the catch I added and rewritten to a 500; (2) my sanitizer collapsed lib/cognito.ts's 14 curated 4xx mappings into that same 500, so a RESET_REQUIRED customer can never delete; (3) my double-tap branch matches UserNotFoundException, which the token-authorized DeleteUser does not return (th
data.why: Four defects from one unattended fix to a security-critical route is the signal to stop, not to patch again. The review's own recommended fixes are architectural and far outside this phase: port the intentionality gate into auth-proxy's lib/utils.ts (fixes 17 other routes), make the shim's invoke-emulator noop() set FunctionError (fixes ~40 call sites), and stop the pre-token trigger minting cognito:groups from the requesting client (fixes 27 grant sites, including the admin fleet's only authorization check). Nothing is deployed - the pin is unmerged - so leaving the regressions costs nothing operationally, while a third unattended pass risks a fifth defect.
data.costIfWrong: The aws main branch carries a delete-account route with four known defects until someone fixes them; anyone who merges the pin without reading the handoff ships them to production.

data.said: The sweep changed one thing materially, so I acted on it rather than just filing it. ## The one that matters beyond this phase `applyCognitoAttributeChanges` has no `is_anonymized` guard — and I verified that `hetzner/workers/reconcile.ts:162` loads that exact handler in-process **every 5 minutes** for any user whose `UserLastModifiedDate` moved. So an anonymized row gets the real name, email and phone written back over `[erased]` within minutes, and `anonymize_customer`'s `AND is_anonymized = false` guard then makes re-erasure a permanent no-op. **This is not confined to the route I was building.** The pre-existing `admin-customer-erasure` endpoint never deletes the Cognito user at all, so every row it has ever anonymized is exposed to the same reversal *today*, in production. That's a live defect this phase surfaced, and it outranks the deploy question the phase was parked on. ## The one I had to correct in my own shipped text My register entry asserted "no tokens are minted on this route." data.what: Android tab icons are <VectorIcon family={MaterialIcons}> via androidSrc, not the 15 template PNGs the plan lists under apps/expo/assets/tabs/.
data.why: The SDK 54 Icon type makes sf and src mutually exclusive (src?: never beside sf) — the plan's 'Icon sf={...} src={...png}' does not typecheck. The real companion prop is androidSrc, and it accepts a React element, so @expo/vector-icons (already shipped with Expo, 14.1.0) gives real vector icons with no binary assets to author, review or keep in sync.
data.costIfWrong: If a MaterialIcons name is wrong, that ANDROID tab renders blank. iOS is unaffected (it reads sf=). Phase 8 should open the app once on an Android emulator to confirm the five names.

data.what: The contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior default for lists is set once on the shared AppFlashList.native.tsx wrapper, not on the two FlashList screen roots the plan names.
data.why: Both roots (all-robots-screen, OrdersListScaffold) render AppFlashList, so one default covers both and any future adopter; the spread still lets a nested list opt out with 'never'. Same reasoning as ScrollView.native.tsx, which the plan itself asks for.
data.costIfWrong: A FlashList nested inside another scroller would double-inset until it passes contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior="never"; neither current root is nested.

data.what: ConfigSection.tsx is NOT a SettingItem consumer — its `Settings` import is the LUCIDE ICON. The only consumer of @my/ui's Settings/SettingItem is drawer-menu/index.tsx. No migration is performed there, and the plan's §Verification line `grep -q MenuRow ... ConfigSection.tsx` is amended to assert the real invariant (no SettingItem reference survives).
data.why: Verified by grep across packages+apps: the only files importing Settings from '@my/ui' are drawer-menu; every other 'Settings,' line sits inside a @tamagui/lucide-icons-2 import. Inserting a MenuRow into a robot-config FORM purely to satisfy a grep would be faking a gate.
data.costIfWrong: If ConfigSection really did contain settings rows, they keep the old look until a later phase notices.

data.what: The settings-tree conversion covers settings/screen.tsx (full MenuGroup+MenuRow rewrite), general-screen.tsx (read-only value rows + the App Lock toggle seated in a MenuGroup) and notifications/PreferencesScreen.tsx (one MenuGroup per category, header=label, footer=description, channel switches as rows). connect-channels/screen.tsx keeps its GlassSurface refract panel and is NOT converted.
data.why: MenuRow is a NAVIGATION row: it owns a chevron, a link/button role and a push. connect-channels §01 is two connect BUTTONS and §02 is a channel status list with per-row disconnect actions on a 'refract' hero panel; MenuGroup exposes no refract, so converting it would strip the web edge-lensing and add nothing. Where a screen genuinely groups settings, the GROUP primitive is applied even though the CONTROL stays a switch — that is the shared vocabulary the phase is for.
data.costIfWrong: connect-channels looks slightly different from the rest of the settings tree; Phase 8's sweep can convert it if the screenshots disagree.

data.what: Exit criterion 3's filters-sheet screenshot and the Profile menu's lower-half screenshot were NOT obtained; the phase hands off in-progress with those two proofs owed. The 23 modal conversions, the menu tree and the ESLint gate ARE done and verified.
data.why: A scroll or swipe that BEGINS on a MenuRow is delivered as a TAP (measured 5x: 'scroll' x2, 700ms swipe, 900ms swipe), so the menu cannot be scrolled to its footer, and the same class of miss made the open-filters tap land on a product card. data.costIfWrong: If the defect is only a Maestro driver artifact rather than app behaviour, Phase 8 spends an hour proving that and the two screenshots cost a further ten minutes.

data.what: deeplinks.sh settles 4s per route, not the 2s the plan's step 1 specifies
data.why: At 2s the screenshot catches the OUTGOING screen: a 51-route sweep produced only 29 distinct frames, with 9 consecutive routes sharing one image. Re-run at 4s, 18/18 consecutive routes moved with zero navigator errors. 2s does not photograph the route it names.
data.costIfWrong: A sweep ~2 min slower; the screenshots are the phase's evidence so a fast-but-wrong frame is worse than a slow one.

data.what: Treated 'every other deep link is ignored' as a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not an app defect, and did not file it as a fix row
data.why: It reproduced twice and looked like a real navigation stall (identical frames + a REPLACE-not-handled toast). A fresh-stack control at 4s settle landed 18/18 with 0 navigator errors, so the stall was the 2s settle. This is Phase 7's stale-bundle lesson in a new costume: a negative result measured through a too-fast probe.
data.costIfWrong: If deep links DO stall at some depth, Phase 9's Danger-zone deep link could be unreachable; the 4s sweep re-runs it every time, so a real stall resurfaces.

data.what: Did NOT apply D1's material=solid escape hatch to /sessions or /marketplace/all-robots
data.why: The plan says switch 'if it hitches'. Measured from the Maestro recordings: both lists hold a MEDIAN 15.0ms frame gap (~66fps). /sessions has the worse tail (p95 46.7ms, 72/595 gaps >33ms = 12.1%) vs all-robots (p95 20.0ms, 27/1232 = 2.2%), but neither sustains a stall — the >500ms outliers are the idle periods between swipes. A simulator VFR capture is not a device performance measurement, so degrading the material on this evidence would trade a documented look for an unproven gain.
data.costIfWrong: If the lists DO hitch on real hardware, /sessions is the one to switch first; the recordings + numbers are in reports/phase-08 so the next session need not re-measure.

data.what: Built, layout-verified and then REVERTED the /sign-in keyboard-avoidance fix (removing the nested FormWrapper); left it for a device/working-keyboard pass
data.why: P6 assigned this fix to Phase 8 and the root cause is written down: sign-in-screen.tsx wraps SchemaForm in a FormWrapper and SchemaForm mounts a second one — on native a FormWrapper IS a KeyboardAwareScrollView, so two nest and the inner content-height one has nothing to scroll. The edit typechecked and the screen rendered identically. But the simulator would NOT raise a software keyboard even with ConnectHardwareKeyboard=0 and a full Simulator restart (r2's stated precondition), so the flow passed VACUOUSLY — the exact vacuous-pass trap that report warns about. Shipping an unverified behavioural change to the app's first screen two phases before release is worse than carrying a known, diagnosed defect.
data.costIfWrong: The defect stays: on a real device the password field sits under the keyboard. Mitigated — P7's auth-email/auth-password/auth-submit testIDs mean flows no longer need coordinate taps, and the exact patch is written in the handoff.
